title: Rational residues, generators and homogeneous independence after localization
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a Noetherian commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], $\varepsilon:A\to k$ a $k$-algebra map, $I=\ker\varepsilon$, and $R$ a localization of $A$ at $I$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] with its compatible $k$-algebra structure. Let $\iota$ be finite and $x_i\in I$. Assume every element of $I$ is a $k$-linear combination of the $x_i$ modulo $I^2$, and every homogeneous degree-$r$ polynomial $f\in k[X_i]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with $f(x)\in I^{r+1}$ is zero. Set $m=IR$ and $z_i=x_i/1$. Then every $a\in R$ has $a-c\in m$ for some $c\in k$, the ideal $m$ is generated by the $z_i$, and for every $r\geq0$ and homogeneous $f$ of degree $r$, $f(z)\in m^{r+1}$ implies $f=0$.

source.place: Proof steps 1–4: the expanded local dimension argument from lem-wf-same-lie-closed-subgroup, clause (2)

proof.text: The map ε is onto by ε(C(c))=c, so I is maximal. For a fraction a/s take c=ε(a)/ε(s); a-C(c)s belongs to I, and multiplication by the unit s/1 shows a/s-C(c) belongs to IR.

Let J be the ideal generated by the x_i. The spanning congruence gives I≤J+I². Mapping ideals gives m≤JR+m². The localized ring is Noetherian and local and m is its maximal ideal. Nakayama applied to the finite ideal m gives m≤JR. The reverse inclusion follows from x_i∈I.

Evaluation commutes with the localization map. If f(z) lies in m^(r+1), clearing denominators gives s f(x) in I^(r+1), s outside I. Mathlib Ideal.IsMaximal.mul_mem_pow shows f(x) lies in I^(r+1), because a power of a maximal ideal is primary. Apply the original independence hypothesis.

theorem homogeneous_independence_localization
    {k A R ι : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [CommRing R] [Algebra A R] [Algebra k R] [IsScalarTower k A R]
    [Fintype ι] (ε : A →ₐ[k] k) [(RingHom.ker ε).IsPrime]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime R (RingHom.ker ε)]
    (x : ι → A) (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ RingHom.ker ε)
    (hspan : ∀ a ∈ RingHom.ker ε, ∃ c : ι → k,
      a - ∑ i, algebraMap k A (c i) * x i ∈ RingHom.ker ε ^ 2)
    (hind : ∀ (r : ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial ι k), f.IsHomogeneous r →
      aeval x f ∈ RingHom.ker ε ^ (r + 1) → f = 0) :
    (∀ a : R, ∃ c : k,
      a - algebraMap k R c ∈ Ideal.map (algebraMap A R) (RingHom.ker ε)) ∧
    Ideal.map (algebraMap A R) (RingHom.ker ε) =
      Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ algebraMap A R (x i))) ∧
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial ι k), f.IsHomogeneous r →
        aeval (fun i ↦ algebraMap A R (x i)) f ∈
          (Ideal.map (algebraMap A R) (RingHom.ker ε)) ^ (r + 1) → f = 0
